deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is the continuation of a draft letter to the 'Lieber Freund' of the previous page, almost certainly Karl Hattendorff. Hattendorff edited Riemann's minimal-surface papers after his death: 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867/68.

The page makes two kinds of statement.

(1) A report of finished calculations.
(a) Riemann says he has carried out the computation for the minimal surface spanned by three straight lines parallel to the three rectangular coordinate axes. The formulas for x, y, z are worked out carefully and expressed in several ways. Among them is a form using logarithms of rational functions and rational functions of one complex variable. In other words, the surface is given by explicitly integrated Weierstrass-type integrals, in his notation with the auxiliary functions X, Y, Z and log-differentials.
(b) He also mentions problems where the surface is bounded by several planes: the 6 faces of a cube or parallelepiped, and the 4 faces of a tetrahedron. He says the computation can be carried through completely in these cases.
In modern terms these are free-boundary (Gergonne-type) or partially free problems for minimal surfaces in polyhedra. The previous page explains the purpose: besides the general skew quadrilateral, whose third-order ODE has an essential constant he could not determine in general, he wanted simple cases where every constant can be determined.

(2) Practical arrangements. He is forced to leave that day by the threatening war; this is the Austro-Prussian war, June 1866. Only since the day before had he had time for their joint work. If Hattendorff wants clarification of any formula, he should note it on the manuscript sheet itself, next to the formula. He should then give the sheet to Riemann's sister, the 'Professorin' (surname uncertain in the image). She will forward it, and Riemann will send his answer back through her. He has to write in pencil. His wife writes his letters, but copying mathematics would cost her endless trouble and not advance the matter.

No derivation is present, so there is nothing to restate step by step. The mathematical content consists of claims of completed results. The details are in the accompanying sheets, which are not on this page.
errors: No mathematical steps to check. The claims that the cube/parallelepiped and tetrahedron cases can be 'completely carried out' are unsubstantiated on this page. Schwarz's later work shows the cube (Gergonne) problem does lead to explicit elliptic/hypergeometric integrals with determinable constants, so the claim is plausible, but no verification is possible here.

results.what: Explicit minimal surface bounded by three straight lines parallel to the three coordinate axes. Coordinates are given via logarithms of rational functions and rational functions of one complex variable.
results.modern_name: Plateau problem for a polygonal (unbounded) boundary solved via the Weierstrass/Riemann representation with conformal mapping (Schwarz–Christoffel-type determination of the Gauss map)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous, ed. Hattendorff 1867); related polygon cases by Schwarz (1865–1872) and Weierstrass (1866)

results.what: Claimed complete solution for minimal surfaces bounded by the faces of a cube/parallelepiped and of a tetrahedron (planar boundary pieces).
results.modern_name: Free-boundary minimal surfaces in polyhedra (Gergonne problem; Schwarz's surfaces in cube/tetrahedron)
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (1872 onward; Gergonne problem posed 1816)

results.what: Historical evidence: Riemann handed his minimal-surface manuscripts to Hattendorff when leaving Göttingen in June 1866 because of the war.
results.modern_name: Provenance of Riemann's posthumous minimal-surface memoir
results.usually_credited_to: Known from Hattendorff's preface and Riemann's biographies (Dedekind)

deep.surprise_reason: The provenance story and the three-lines example are known from Hattendorff's 1867 edition. The more notable point is the bare claim that Riemann could fully handle cube/parallelepiped faces and tetrahedron faces. That is the territory later associated with Schwarz's work on the Gergonne problem in the cube and on tetrahedral boundaries. But it is a one-line assertion in a letter, with no formulas on this page, so the surprise stays modest.

checkable.asserts: The Weierstrass/Riemann integrand components (1-g^2, i(1+g^2), 2g) are isotropic (sum of squares = 0). This is the condition underlying Riemann's representation of minimal surfaces by functions of one complex variable, which he is using for the three-lines and polyhedral cases.

transcription_corrections: Line 'In diesen Fällen glaubt [?] sich die Rechnung vollständig durchführen': the verb is 'läßt' ('läßt sich die Rechnung vollständig durchführen'), not 'glaubt'.
'für mehrere ebene [?] Flächen' may read 'für mehrere ebene Flächen' or 'endliche Flächen'; the image is ambiguous ('...[e]ndliche Fläche').
The interlinear insertion above 'finden' transcribed '{+bestimmt ausgedrückt [?]+}' is quite uncertain in the image; it may be something like 'verschiedenartig ...'.
'der Professorin Bach [?]': the surname is uncertain in the image and should stay marked as doubtful.
'auf demselben [?] Manuscript': the image supports 'dies auf dem Manuscript' or similar; 'demselben' is doubtful.
